title: Minimum Deletions to Make Alternating Substring
summary: Given a string s of length n consisting only of the characters 'A' and 'B', and a 2D integer array queries of length q , where each queries[i] is one of the following: - [1, j]: Flip the character at index j of s .
statement: Given a string s of length n consisting only of the characters 'A' and 'B', and a 2D integer array queries of length q , where each queries[i] is one of the following: - [1, j]: Flip the character at index j of s . This operation changes 'A' to 'B' and 'B' to 'A' and affects subsequent queries. - [2, l, r]: Compute the minimum number of character deletions required to make the substring s[l..r] alternating. This operation does not modify s ; the length of s remains n . A substring is considered alternating if no two adjacent characters are the same. A substring of length 1 is always considered alternating. Return an integer array answer , where answer[i] is the result of the i -th query of type [2, l, r].
constraints: s contains up to 100,000 A/B characters and there are up to 100,000 queries.
[1,j] flips s[j]; [2,l,r] asks for the minimum deletions in the current substring.
Return answers only for type-two queries.
hints: For a binary string, one deletion is needed for each equal adjacent pair in the retained interval.
Store equality indicators for boundaries (i-1,i) in a Fenwick tree.
A flip changes only boundaries j and j+1; a range answer sums boundaries l+1 through r.
Runs of equal characters contribute length minus one, exactly matching their required deletions, and runs add independently.
editorial: Runs of equal characters contribute length minus one, exactly matching their required deletions, and runs add independently.

tests.explanation: BA is already alternating; after the flip the full string is AAA and needs two deletions.
ABB needs one deletion, then flipping the last character makes ABA need zero.
